notes.text: Maxim Tsyplakov has not dressed for the last 6 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. William Strömgren has taken his spot beside Adam Klapka and Jonathan Castagna.
Connor Zary is out (knee surgery) and has missed the last 17 games.

Kevin Bahl is out for the season and has missed the last 4 games. Joel Hanley has taken his spot beside Šimon Nemec. That pair has had 33% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 50:42 together, down from 46% with Bahl.
Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 20 games, up from 2% last season.

stakes: The Flames go in tied for fifth in the Pacific with 19 points, 2 points behind the Ducks, third. A regulation win for the Flames would pull them level with the Ducks.

story.head: Carlsson’s favorite opponent
paras: The Ducks have won two of the three meetings this season. The Flames (9-10-1) beat Los Angeles 3-2 last night, while the Ducks (10-9-1) lost 6-2 to the Islanders the same night. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Flames sixth (tied for 23rd in the NHL) and the Ducks third (18th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

The Flames take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd) and have struggled on the power play (31st). Calgary has scored 2.50 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. As for the Ducks, they are one of the league’s most physical teams (2nd), hound the puck on the forecheck (3rd) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (31st). Anaheim has allowed 3.80 goals a game, the third most in the league. The Flames are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Ducks. On top of that, both teams like to play fast, especially the Flames (2nd), so expect an open game.

Joel Farabee (7 G / 10 A / 17 P in 20 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, and Matt Coronato (4 G / 11 A / 15 P in 20 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Ducks, Leo Carlsson (6 G / 21 A / 27 P in 20 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in seven straight games against Calgary. Cutter Gauthier (17 G / 7 A / 24 P in 19 GP) has a team-high 17 goals, tied for second in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games.
Devin Cooley (5-4-0 / .913 SV% in 9 GS) has been a rock in net for Calgary and is expected to start. Ville Husso (2-3-0 / .869 SV% in 4 GS) has struggled for Anaheim so far, but is expected to start.
